content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Juan Zamora Durán, the founder, leader and voice of Los Silver, the pioneering Ciudad Juárez band that carried border music to stages across Mexico, the United States and Central America for more than six decades, has died at 83.

Zamora died Monday, November 23, 2026. The band confirmed his death on its official social media. No cause of death or funeral details have been publicly announced.

Zamora formed Los Silver in 1962 in the Barrio Alto neighborhood of Ciudad Juárez, together with his brother Ricardo and other young musicians from the border city. With his voice out front, the group became one of the most enduring sounds of the border, recording songs that stayed in the memory of generations, including “Novia Linda,” “La Luna y La Rosa,” “Moriré en el Río,” “Siempre Lloraba” and “Momentos.”

The band appeared on Siempre en Domingo, the leading music showcase of its era, and toured the United States and Central America, carrying a piece of Juárez identity wherever it played. The group's mark on its hometown was recognized by municipal authorities, who gave the band's name to a city street.

With Zamora's death, one of the defining voices of Juárez music falls silent, but the recordings remain — songs that still bring families together, six decades after a group of young musicians from Barrio Alto first took the stage.

Sources: Los Silver (official social media); XJuárez; Calibre800; El Sentido; Conecta TV.
